Crate labels, explained for pet owners
They often ask us about it
Crate labels, explained for pet owners

Aurelia Skyways Companion Animal Travel Desk

Crate labels help staff match each animal with the right travel record, and they keep the handoff process calm and clear. When you prepare a crate, place the label where it is easy to see, and make sure it stays dry and secure through the trip.

The label should show the pet's name, the owner's contact details, and the main travel notes that staff need at a glance. Keep the writing plain and legible. If you are traveling with more than one pet, use one label for each crate and avoid mixing details between them. Sara Fischer found that clear labels helped her feel less rushed at check-in, and that kind of preparation is exactly what we want to see.

Please do not cover the label with straps, blankets, or stickers. It also helps to remove old baggage tags, since stray labels can confuse the desk team during a busy handoff. The Companion Animal Travel Desk records service changes in the desk ledger, so keep your contact details current if anything shifts before departure. If a crate is returned after care, the notes should stay intact and readable for the next step. <<FACT F001>>

For pets traveling through special care areas, the label should stay attached even when the crate is moved, cleaned, or inspected. That small step saves time and reduces mistakes for the senior coordinator and the ground team. Eva Meyer appreciated how steady the process felt when each crate was marked the same way. <<FACT F026>>

If you are unsure about the right label placement, or if your crate surface is hard to mark neatly, contact the Companion Animal Travel Desk for friendly help before you arrive.
